account:
Today seems largely routine, with no confirmed emergency or unusual gathering. During my market walk the baker said the stall held thirty-two fresh loaves and reported no town problem or confirmed gathering order. Several townspeople repeated sightings of the baker carrying a sack of bread at the inn and plaza; I do not know the purpose of those deliveries. My neighbour says some residents mistook an oven's glow for celebration lights, but the baker explained it was ordinary baking. I have no evidence of a celebration.

The builder apparently knows of my request for a road, bridge and lamp inspection, according to my neighbour. I have not received findings or an estimate. My neighbour has noticed no damage, but has not inspected properly and cannot judge lamps in daylight. They offered to pass specific problems to the builder. They also report, secondhand from freight, a quiet warehouse and an available ferry.

Town accounts remain unresolved: the secretary had no ledgers or bills and did not know where accounts were kept. I checked the treasury, found 128 emeralds and no records, and left the funds untouched. I asked the secretary to locate existing accounts rather than invent unsupported figures.

The secretary confirmed my usual three o'clock tea at the east-bank cottage. I attended and exchanged local news with my neighbour. I am now leaving for the 16:30 office appointment, with home scheduled for 19:00. Nothing I have heard establishes a hidden purpose behind today's ordinary bread supply, freight activity or friendly visits.
